To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a conserved S40 residue in p6 is involved in HIV-1 budding and that its mutation affects the interaction with Alix, a known late domain binding protein.
S40 in HIV-1 p6 impacts local (L domain-1 and -2, Gag-Alix, and CA NTD) and distal (PR) budding determinants and reveals additional late domain activities.

a conserved S40 residue in p6 of HIV-1 GAG is a novel late domain that regulates budding through multiple mechanisms, including by affecting interactions with Alix, and by modulating CA-SP1 processing and membrane curvature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel late domain activities and with the elucidation of the mechanisms of their action in HIV-1 budding.
the identification of new determinants of HIV-1 budding and with the understanding of the mechanisms that regulate HIV-1 particle formation.
the identification of a novel budding determinant in HIV-1 p6 and with the characterization of its impact on the function of the other late domain activities in the viral budding machinery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S40F mutation affects the budding process by perturbing Gag p6 interactions with Tsg101, Alix, and the capsid N-terminal domain.
the S40F mutation impacts all of the budding determinants in HIV-1, revealing additional activities in the Gag p6 late domain.
the S40F substitution in GAG p6 results in a novel HIV-1 late domain activity that impacts local and distant budding determinants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S40F mutation impacts multiple budding determinants, including L domain-1, L domain-2, CA N-terminal domain and Gag-Alix binding, revealing additional activities of the p6 late domain.
S40 is an important regulator of late domain functions in the HIV-1 Gp41p6 protein.

the S40F substitution results in a more open conformation of the G6-G6’ hairpin, which in turn impacts the function of the L domain-1, the Gag-CA interaction and the Gag-Alix binding, all of which are required for HIV-1 budding.
The main takeaway from our work is that

S40F, which is the most common polymorphism at this site in the human population, has the potential to impact viral infectivity and therefore could be a factor that influences the transmission and spread of HIV-1.

the S40F mutation, by perturbing Gag-Alix and Gag-CA interactions, uncovers additional L domain activities and reveals the interdependence of L domain and other Gag determinants in the budding process.
the S40F mutation, which does not alter the pol sequence, impacts budding mediated through all three of the known L domains, as well as the CA N-terminal domain.
